subject: Exit orchestration & bespoke order-form: scope and timelines

Cc: Apex Biotech - Legal <legal@apexbiotech.com>

Subject: Exit orchestration request — bespoke residency/delete windows

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we get into contracting, Legal and IT have two asks we want reflected in the Order Form / SLA addendum:

1) We need a defined cross-region deletion window for replicated data. If a deletion is requested, we need confirmation that copies in backups/replicas will be removed within X days and a certification of deletion.
2) For certain regulated artifacts (PHI-derived vectors), Apex requires a 90-day escrow window after contract termination where data is quarantined but not accessible, followed by verifiable deletion across all tiers.

Can you propose language / a timeline and call out any operational constraints (snapshots, backups, snapshot retention, crypto key destruction)? Also include any lead times and pricing if this is outside standard order forms.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — Legal would like to see redlineable language this week.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of IT, Apex Biotech

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a proposed Order Form addendum outline and operational notes. I'll loop Legal for precise wording but wanted to get concrete timelines on the table for negotiation.

Proposed addendum (high level):
- Scope: Applies to customer data, derivatives (embeddings, vector indices), and associated logs/snapshots created while the account was active. Excludes telemetry anonymized metrics unless explicitly included.
- Residency & deletion guarantee: Upon receipt of a formal data deletion request (post-contract termination or earlier if invoked):
  * Logical deletion (application-level removal) enacted within 24 hours of request acknowledgement.
  * Persistent data and replicas: full purge of active replicas within 7 calendar days for same-region copies, 14 calendar days for cross-region replicas (this accounts for replication and scheduled replication windows).
  * Snapshot/backups: coordinated expiration sweep to remove snapshots within 30 calendar days; if snapshots are stored on third-party cloud backup, deletion can require up to 45 calendar days depending on provider SLA.
- Escrow/quarantine: Optional 90-day quarantine option (Apex requested) — data remains logically inaccessible to both parties, preserved in isolated storage tagged for deletion at end of the escrow term.
- Crypto/key destruction: For cryptographically sharded keys we will perform key destruction within 48 hours of final deletion events and provide a signed certificate of key destruction.
- Certification: Redwood will provide a deletion certificate and an audit report (hash of deleted artifact lists, deletion timestamps, and node identifiers) within 10 business days of completion.
- Legal hold: Redwood will pause any automated deletion while a court/legal hold is in effect; customer must provide formal hold notice.
- Pricing: Escrow/quarantine incurs a monthly fee (TBD); accelerated snapshot purge (under 30 days) is a paid option.
- Exceptions & lead time: Some third-party backup providers require 30 days notice for deletion. Redwood may require a 5-business-day lead time for large-scale (>50TB) coordinated purges.

Operational caveats:
- Replication lag: cross-region replication and eventual consistency mean absolute simultaneity across all nodes is not guaranteed; timelines are expressed as completion windows.
- Audit artifacts: we retain deletion logs and a minimal metadata trail for 180 days after deletion certificate for auditability unless Apex requests truncation earlier (subject to compliance regs).

I'm attaching a draft addendum and a template deletion certification for your review. Laura/Rishi — please weigh in on the wording where I flagged Legal/Compliance.

Next steps: Emma — can you confirm if Apex expects the escrow to be charged or billed as part of termination? Also confirm whether PHI-derived vectors are to be explicitly scoped as "regulated artifacts" in the addendum.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Emma / Jonas,

Thanks Jonas — this is a solid starting point. A few suggested legal clarifications to include in the addendum text:

- Definitions: Define "deletion" vs "destruction" vs "quarantine/escrow" explicitly. The certificate should reference the identifiers we are deleting (bucket prefixes, vector index ids, snapshot ids) and the UTC deletion timestamps.
- Burden of proof: Redwood will certify deletion but cannot guarantee irrecoverability for copies stored outside Redwood control (third-party cloud backups) beyond the stated provider deletion windows.
- Audit scope: The deletion certificate will include scope, checksum lists, timestamps, the operator id, and the digest of the S3/Blob objects removed where applicable.
- Data mapping: We should require Apex to provide a data mapping matrix for the 90-day escrow items so we can uniquely identify records. If no mapping is provided, Redwood will apply a best-effort mapping and reserve the right to charge for manual reconciliation.
- Fees and credits: Add a clause for cost of expedited snapshot purge and separately the monthly fee for escrow. Provide an estimate band in an appendix.

Rishi — quick note on metrics retention: we should confirm the earlier note that we retain only minimal deletion metadata for 180 days; if Apex wants shorter retention we need to confirm compliance implications.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Li <emma.li@apexbiotech.com>

Subject: Re: Exit orchestration request — bespoke residency/delete windows

Laura/Jonas — helpful, thanks. A few clarifications from our side:

- Apex confirms the escrow will be charged as a pass-through to our SOW (we need invoice line items).
- PHI-derived vectors should be scoped as "regulated artifacts" and listed in Appendix A — we will provide the mapping matrix by Friday.
- For cryptographic key destruction: we require an HSM-backed key destruction certificate. Can Redwood commit to HSM-backed key material removal for keys used to encrypt PHI-derived artifacts?
- Snapshots: our security team insists on a maximum 21-day window for snapshot purge in same-provider clouds (we understand this may be an expedited option). Please provide the expedited pricing option in the addendum.

If you can update the draft with these points we can circulate to Procurement + Legal for a redline.

—Emma

Emma / team — great, noted. Summary of agreed updates and immediate next steps: 

1) Escrow billing: will be added as a monthly SOW line item; Finance will provide an estimate band in the appendix.
2) PHI-derived vectors: will be explicitly called out as "regulated artifacts" and referenced to Appendix A (awaiting your mapping matrix).
3) HSM-backed key destruction: Redwood confirms use of customer- or Redwood-managed HSM for key material used to encrypt PHI artifacts; we will provide a signed HSM key destruction certificate.
4) Snapshot purge: expedited same-provider purge to 21 calendar days is available as a paid option; standard window remains 30 calendar days.
5) Certification: deletion certificate + audit digest will be delivered within 10 business days post-completion.

I attached the updated addendum (v1.1) and the deletion cert template for redline. Next actions from Redwood: Laura will produce legal-ready clause language, Finance will add an appendix with estimated fees, and Solutions will insert operational steps.
